description:
Hello from Uruguay! 🇺🇾🚀

We are BJFL, a team of students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay, excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🌎✨
summary: HealthVest is a wearable vest made from recycled materials that monitors an astronaut’s health and surroundings in real time. Our team, BJFL, built it using a BBC micro:bit and the Elecfreaks Smart Health Kit. The vest uses sensors to measure body and cabin temperature and humidity, ultraviolet light exposure, and the astronaut’s movement, and it can detect a fall or sudden impact. All the readings appear on a small screen on the vest, so astronauts can check their status at a glance, and the vest can warn them when something is wrong. NASA monitors astronauts’ health constantly, and on long missions to the Moon and Mars, crews will need simple, reliable tools to take care of themselves far from Earth. By using recycled materials, our vest also shows that space technology can be sustainable and low-cost.
details:
What it does and how it works. The micro:bit is the “brain” of the vest. It reads data from several sensors and shows the results on an OLED screen attached to the front of the vest:

  1. Temperature and humidity sensor (DHT11): checks if the astronaut is too hot or too cold.
  2. UV sensor: measures exposure to ultraviolet light.
  3. Accelerometer (built into the micro:bit): tracks movement and activity, and detects falls or strong impacts.
  4. Crash sensor: works as an emergency button the astronaut can press to ask for help.
  5. Fan: turns on automatically to cool the astronaut if the temperature gets too high.
  6. Rainbow LED: shows colors as alerts (for example, green when everything is fine and red when there is a problem).
dataRefs: NASA: Wearable Tech for Space Station Research
